intuition: Place one queen in each row. Before choosing a column, check whether another queen already uses that column or either diagonal. If no later row can be filled, remove the last queen and try a different column. This avoids exploring boards that already contain an attack.

A queen at (row,col) occupies one column and two diagonals. Squares share the descending diagonal precisely when row-col is equal, and share the ascending diagonal when row+col is equal. Three sets make each safety check immediate. The placement list remembers only selected columns, postponing string construction until a complete board exists.

Backtracking means that these occupancy marks belong to one branch, not to the whole search. After exploring a queen’s descendants, remove its column and diagonals before trying the next column. This restoration makes each sibling start from the same parent board.
Reaching row n certifies a complete legal arrangement; reaching a row with no safe column simply closes a failed branch.

steps: With n=4, try row 0, column 0. Later rows cannot complete a safe board, so that branch is undone.
Try row 0, column 1. At row 1, column 0 shares the ascending diagonal and column 1 is occupied, so keep searching.
With row 0 at column 1, row 1 column 2 is rejected: both queens have row-col=-1 and share a descending diagonal. Column 3 passes all three occupancy checks.
Row 2 then uses column 0, and row 3 uses column 2. Placement [1,3,0,2] is a complete board.
Emit [".Q..","...Q","Q...","..Q."], then undo the last choices so the search can continue.
The mirrored placement [2,0,3,1] gives the second board. All remaining branches fail, so exactly two boards are returned.

codeNotes.code: if col in columns or row - col in descending or row + col in ascending:
codeNotes.note: These three occupied-coordinate tests cover every attack not already ruled out by one queen per row.
Recursion advances to a new row only after recording a safe queen; every recursive prefix is therefore legal.
Removing the choice and its three occupancy marks is what makes later sibling branches independent.

keyDecision: A placement is safe only when its column and both diagonal identifiers are unused.

concept.question: How can a queen placement prune every board that already contains an attack?
intuition: Trying every arrangement before checking attacks explores many doomed boards. Once two queens share a column or diagonal, later placements cannot repair their conflict.

Place one queen in each row. Remember occupied columns and the two kinds of diagonal. Explore only squares that avoid all three. When later rows have no safe square, remove the last queen and try another route.
concept.observation: A new queen must share neither a column nor either diagonal with an earlier queen.
approach: Choose a safe column in the next row.
Record its column and diagonals, then continue to the following row.
Save a full board, or undo a placement when exploring another branch.
concept.correctness: At each depth, all placed queens are mutually nonattacking. Adding a square outside occupied columns and diagonals preserves that fact. Every valid complete board supplies a legal next square in every row, so its route is explored. Undoing placements restores earlier availability. Complete routes are exactly valid boards.

complexity.explanation: The search may explore factorially many row choices before pruning. Current placements and occupied-line records use linear auxiliary memory, while returning every board requires its full output storage.

pitfalls: Remove all occupancy records when undoing.
Return complete boards, not merely queen coordinates.

scenes.title: A corner route fails
scenes.narration: On a four-by-four board, beginning at the top-left corner cannot lead to a complete safe placement. Return to the first row.
scenes.decision: A dead end invalidates that branch, not the entire problem.

scenes.title: A complete safe route
scenes.narration: Choose columns 1,3,0,2 in successive rows. No two queens share a column or diagonal.
scenes.decision: One queen per row already rules out horizontal attacks.

scenes.title: The mirror is the second route
scenes.narration: Columns 2,0,3,1 give the other complete board. Exhausting the legal branches yields exactly two solutions.
scenes.decision: All safe choices are explored after earlier choices are undone.

scenes.title: A boundary to remember
scenes.narration: Boundary example: a one-by-one board has one valid queen placement. Boards of sizes two and three have no complete safe arrangement.
